headline: Domain priors paired with flow and diffusion generators for DNA and single-cell data
label: Generative Models For Biomolecules
summary: Recent preprints inject biological priors, rewards, and metadata conditioning into generative DNA, protein, and single-cell models.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generative or latent modeling in which biological structure enters through reward, conditioning, or priors rather than sample likelihood alone. PlasmidGPT compares SFT and GRPO post-training of a whole-plasmid DNA language model under a biologically motivated reward. CLOP-DiT aligns BiomedBERT text with scGPT cell embeddings and conditions a diffusion transformer on structured metadata to generate single-cell expression. Two Dirichlet-prior autoencoder preprints add flow-matching refinement to scRNA-seq representation learning; one reports improved cluster geometry at the cost of label recovery, while Topic-FM yields interpretable topic-gene signatures. The novelty lies in pairing domain-specific priors with flow-based or diffusion-based machinery across DNA and single-cell modalities. AINN-P1 and co-distilled ESM models instead address sequence-only protein fitness prediction. All evidence is preprint-based and provisional, and none establishes generalization beyond reported benchmarks.
